correctness.rationale: The independent small-jump martingale has variance rate \(2c(\delta L)^{2-\alpha}/(2-\alpha)\); Doob at an exponential time gives (2). The large-jump process has two-event probability \(O(L^{-2\alpha})\), and the width-epsilon exit-band has probability \(O(\varepsilon L^{-\alpha})\), establishing the marked single-excursion measure asymptotic. An independent exponential restart clock supplies the exact geometric-renewal identity; numerator and denominator expansions yield the full joint Laplace-mark limit. All quantifiers fix alpha, sigma, r, Lambda; 0<alpha<2 controls the vanishing small-jump error. Bounded continuous test functions and tail truncation justify weak convergence. Code checks normalizations only.

value.rationale: The question arises directly from a recently established large-interval mean law. Its answer completely specifies the location and size of the final jump on the natural scale, the sign bias from an asymmetric reset point, and asymptotic independence from the waiting time. Mean/time-only first-passage formulas cannot determine these spatial marks, and the universal power-law overshoot is qualitatively different from continuous boundary exit.
